title: Procedural CV-babble vocal synth — Animal-Crossing-style speech-like utterances per emotion slot
intent: Each bomber emits a short SPEECH-LIKE utterance at five emotional moments (place-bomb, hit-survived, pickup, death, victory). NOT a single grunt — a multi-syllable phrase that the listener parses as 'this character is talking', the way Animal Crossing's animalese reads as speech even though no real words exist. Each utterance is 2–5 syllables, each syllable is a consonant transient (10–30 ms) + a formant-shaped vowel pulse (40–100 ms), scheduled via Web Audio with an inter-syllable gap (10–40 ms) that produces conversational cadence. Per-bomber voice colour (10 seed-derived knobs) gives identity; per-slot phrase tables give emotion. Zero audio assets — pure synthesis. Supersedes the single-envelope direction in `docs/research/voice-synth-research.md` per the design override in `docs/game-design/voice-synth-design.md`.
rationale: User feedback 2026-05-22 explicitly rejected the single-grunt direction (paraphrased: the user wants the sounds the characters emit to feel like actual words, similar to Animal Crossing's animalese — where the player almost recognises speech without any real words being said). The dev research artifact (`docs/research/voice-synth-research.md`) correctly identified source-filter formant synth as the per-vowel primitive but capped scope at a single envelope per slot — that produces 'this robot beeped', not 'this character spoke'. Multi-syllable cadence is what triggers the speech-recognition heuristic in the listener's brain; spectral content alone doesn't. This story keeps every technical recommendation of the dev research that wasn't about utterance length and overrides only the multi-syllable exclusion. Full design rationale + reference matrix (8 known approaches, 5 rejected with reasons) lives in `docs/game-design/voice-synth-design.md`.
acceptanceHints: READ FIRST: `docs/game-design/voice-synth-design.md` is the source of truth for the synth shape — slot phrase tables, knob ranges, override list against the dev research. This story is the implementation contract for what that doc specifies.
Dependencies: existing audio-fx.ts graph + contextFactory test seam (already in repo). NO new audio framework, NO new bundle dependencies.
examples/kaboom-crew/src/voice-synth.ts: NEW pure module. Three primary exports:
voiceColourFromSeed(seed: number): VoiceColour — derives 10 knobs from recipe.seed via xorshift32. Deterministic.

planUtterance(colour: VoiceColour, slot: VoiceSlot): SyllableSchedule[] — pure, returns the explicit schedule (start times in ms, consonant/vowel specs per syllable, pitch contour). NO AudioContext dependency — fully unit-testable.
emitUtterance(ctx: AudioContext, schedule: SyllableSchedule[]): void — only function that touches Web Audio. Schedules all nodes via ctx.currentTime + offsets.
10 SEED-DERIVED VOICE KNOBS (recipe.voice block — extends the CharacterRecipe schema, ~45 bytes JSON):
basePitchHz       : 90..260   — base oscillator frequency
formantF1Hz       : 300..900  — first formant
formantF2Hz       : 1200..2400 — second formant
formantQ          : 4..12     — filter resonance
vibratoHz         : 0..8      — vibrato rate
vibratoDepth      : 0..0.04   — vibrato depth
noiseMix          : 0..0.4    — gravel / breath
phrasePaceMultiplier : 0.6..1.4 — multiplies the slot's gap-ms (low = fast talker, high = slow drawl)
consonantStyle    : 0..1      — 0 = pure noise transient, 0.5 = mixed, 1 = pitched click (drives 'soft' vs 'hard' articulation)
vowelDriftAmount  : 0..0.3    — multiplier on the slot's per-syllable F1/F2 deltas; 0 = monotone vowel, 0.3 = pronounced vowel variation (drives 'expressiveness')
5 SLOT PHRASE TABLES (fixed, NOT seed-derived — they're the EMOTION layer):
place-bomb: 3 syllables, flat pitch contour (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), 20 ms gap, vowel deltas (0,0)→(0,+200)→(-100,0) — neutral 'bi-da-bo'
hit:        2 syllables, contour (1.0, 0.7), 15 ms gap, vowel deltas (+150,+200)→(0,-100) — sharp 'wha-OO!'
pickup:     3 syllables, contour (1.0, 1.15, 1.3) rising, 18 ms gap, deltas (0,+300)→(-50,+100)→(-100,0) — 'yi-pi-pa!'
SYLLABLE SUB-UNIT SPEC:

Consonant transient (optional, 10–30 ms): one of {b/d/g/p/t/k/m/n/w/y} families. b/d/g/p/t/k → noise burst (5 ms white noise via BufferSource → bandpass at 2–4 kHz → 25 ms envelope). m/n → low-pass pitched pulse. w/y → pitched glide into vowel. Selection per-syllable from seed-derived hash. consonantStyle knob biases noise-vs-pitched mix.

Vowel pulse (40–100 ms): sawtooth oscillator at current pitch (basePitch × slot's contour multiplier × (1 + vibrato modulation)) → 2 parallel BiquadFilter bandpass at F1, F2 (colour knobs + slot vowel-delta × vowelDriftAmount) → gain envelope (5 ms attack, peak, decay to silence). Q from formantQ knob.
Inter-syllable gap: silence — no nodes scheduled, just a time offset. gap = slot.gap × phrasePaceMultiplier.

UTTERANCE TOTAL LENGTH per slot: roughly 250–600 ms depending on syllable count + pace. Falls within the gameplay tick budget (no slot blocks any system); fits below the auto-restart's 3-second post-death window with comfortable room.
EVENT WIRING — audio-fx.ts gains FIVE new event names, fired alongside the existing clip events:
play('voice-place-bomb', { entityId }) — fires when BombPlacementSystem successfully spawns a bomb. Existing 'bomb-place' clip still plays in parallel; voice is additive in different spectral band.
play('voice-hit',         { entityId }) — fires when a shielded bomber survives a blast (depends on GDP-2026-05-22-006 Shield landing first; without it, this event has no trigger — fine).
play('voice-pickup',      { entityId }) — fires when PickupCollectSystem applies a pickup. Existing 'pickup' clip still plays.

play('voice-death',       { entityId }) — fires on alive=false flip. Timed to start ~50 ms into the ragdoll launch (so the listener hears the impact + immediately the death voice; matches the perception of 'they got hit and yelped').
play('voice-victory',     { entityId }) — fires once per round on the WINNING bomber when RoundState.phase flips to 'won'. ONE bomber wins → ONE voice fires.
BOT vs PLAYER VOICE BIAS (closes characters-and-visual.md §7.1 open question):

voiceColourFromSeed knows if the entity has a BotBrain component (passed as second arg). Bot-flagged entities shift waveform pool toward harsher timbres + higher pitch (300–480 Hz); player entities lean smoother + lower (180–380 Hz). Same recipe seed still wins for individual identity; the bias just colours the family.

ACCESSIBILITY KNOB: `?vocals=off` URL flag (top-level, NOT in recipe — accessibility is a player setting, not character identity). Mutes the synth without affecting other audio. Robot-playtest recordings can use this for clean audio capture.
UNIT TESTS:
voiceColourFromSeed deterministic: 200 random seeds → identical outputs across two calls. All 10 knob values inside declared ranges.
planUtterance deterministic: every (colour, slot) pair returns bit-identical SyllableSchedule across two calls.
planUtterance shape invariants: place-bomb has exactly 3 syllables, death has exactly 4, victory has exactly 5, etc. (locks the slot patches against accidental drift).
Bot bias: 200 random bot-seeds → ≥ 80% pick saw OR triangle waveform; 200 random player-seeds → ≥ 60% pick sine OR triangle.
Snapshot test: voiceColour for seed=1 matches a frozen reference (catches accidental algorithm drift).
contextFactory seam: planUtterance has zero AudioContext references; emitUtterance is the only function that needs the seam-injected fake context for testing scheduling.
INTEGRATION TESTS:
audio-fx.ts smoke: each of the 5 new events produces ≥ 1 scheduled node call under the fake context (proves wiring).
Mute test: `?vocals=off` → emitUtterance is a no-op; existing clip path unaffected.
PLAYTEST QA BAR (manual, documented in PR notes — these are user-perception checks, not assertions):
Two bombers with seeds 1 + 42 play a round. Blindfolded listener identifies WHICH bomber just placed a bomb based on voice alone (≥ 70% accuracy over 10 events).
Same bomber's pickup vs death vs victory voices are distinguishable by emotion alone (rising / falling / sustained).
When asked to describe the audio, a non-Russian-speaking listener says 'they're speaking' or 'they're talking', not 'they're beeping'. (This is the user's actual ask — the QA bar in plain words.)
PERFORMANCE:
Per utterance: 2–5 syllables × (1 oscillator + 2 filters + optional noise burst + gain) = ~20 audio nodes scheduled, all torn down within 600 ms. Negligible.
Bundle: ~250 LOC of new code; the slot phrase tables are ~50 lines of const data. Still under the 10 KB synth bundle budget from voice-synth-research.md §1.
Cap simultaneous utterances at 4 — extras drop silently (mirrors the dev research's cap, applied here per-utterance not per-syllable).
WHAT THIS STORY EXPLICITLY OVERRIDES from `docs/research/voice-synth-research.md` §6:
Research said: 'Multi-syllable utterances. Each slot is one envelope.' — REJECTED.

Research said: 'No words, no phonemes, no language.' — PARTIALLY REJECTED: still no intelligible language, but vowel-like phonemes and consonant-like transients are required for the speech-cadence effect.
Everything else in voice-synth-research.md §1–5 + §7–9 is authoritative and unchanged.
OUT OF SCOPE (this story will NOT do):
Real intelligible speech / actual words.
Lip sync (no mouth socket on the bomber mesh).
Per-event variation within a session — same bomber on the same slot ALWAYS sounds identical (deterministic for replay + network).
Voice-actor pipeline / pre-recorded samples.
Multi-language support (vowel formants are Peterson & Barney American English; non-verbal babble doesn't need localisation).
Per-bomber phrase length variation — all bombers use the same syllable count for the same slot in v1.
Stuttering / hesitation patterns mid-phrase.
Voice-fade-under-blast (side-chain ducking) — implement only if playtest shows voice masked by simultaneous blast SFX.
